Κλασική Μουσική

Ρεσιτάλ Κιθάρας του Δημήτρη Κουρζάκη

Παρασκευή 13 Φεβρουαρίου στις 00:00 | ΑΙΘΟΥΣΑ ΣΥΝΑΥΛΙΩΝ ΦΙΛΙΠΠΟΣ ΝΑΚΑΣ

The silence in the Filippos Nakas concert hall holds a particular quality. Acoustic panels designed for exactly this purpose absorb everything except the music. You settle into your seat as Dimitris Kourzakis prepares his guitar. No amplification. Just wood, strings, and technique.

Classical guitar recital demands absolute attention from performer and audience alike. The instrument's intimate voice requires a room designed to carry its subtleties — the way nails meet strings, the resonance of the body, the decay of notes into silence. Kourzakis brings years of study and performance to this exposed format where every choice is audible.

The audience for classical guitar tends toward the knowledgeable. These are listeners who understand the difficulty hidden within apparent simplicity, who can hear the difference between competent and compelling. Many studied the instrument themselves; others simply learned to listen carefully. The shared attention creates a quality of silence that supports rather than pressures.

Filippos Nakas Conservatory provides the acoustic environment this music requires. The hall was built for solo instrumental performance, with dimensions that allow the guitar's full voice to develop without artificial assistance. When Kourzakis plays a pianissimo passage, it reaches the back row. When he attacks a chord, it doesn't overwhelm.

If you need drama and spectacle, solo guitar recital operates at different scale. The rewards here come from subtlety — the slight rubato that shapes a phrase, the voicing that brings out an inner line. But if you're ready to hear classical guitar in conditions that reveal its true character, where the performer has nowhere to hide and nothing to hide behind — Nakas provides the setting.
